newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money remains high on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money remains high on tight liquidity.

text.p: Jakarta call money remained high on the back of sustained tight liquidity in the money market.
Overnight money was traded at 20.0/21.0 percent in the morning as the central bank maintained a tight short-term money policy, dealers said.
They said Bank Indonesia drained some 149 billion rupiah from the money market while keeping short-term rates expensive and scrapped the auction of short-term securities (SBPUs).
"The market is still tight. I think we are going to live with it in the near-term until we see some stability in the foreign exchange market," one dealer said.
The central bank kept its overnight rates of bilateral SBIs unchanged but raised its two-to-four day papers by 300 basis points.

The bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, two-to-four day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
Longer-term rates were driven higher by expensive short-term money and rises in the swap market. One- and three-month money were both at 18.5/19.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 19.62 percent, compared with 18.75 percent on Thursday.
